proposition.claim:
Equation reference: eq:qbound. Fix an even integer \(k\ge2\). The density \(\mathcal M_k(y)\), for \(y>0\), is defined in Theorem 1. Its weights in Theorem 3 are \[A_p=p^4-2p^2-p+1,\qquad
 Q(d)=\mu^2(d)\prod_{p\mid d}\frac{p^2}{A_p}.\] The constants \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) have the paper’s normalization. In particular \(\alpha>0\), \(Q(1)=1\), \(Q(d)\ge0\), and \[
 Q(d)\ll d^{-2},\] because \(\prod_p p^4/A_p\) converges: every factor is positive and \(1+O(p^{-2})\). None of the arguments below changes the normalization of the standard Bessel function \(J_\nu\).

For the conditional argument, RH has exactly the meaning used in Lemma 7.3: the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function have real part \(1/2\). Theorem 6 additionally assumes fixed \(c>1\) and even \(k\ge6\). For Proposition 3.1, \(P>2\) is prime, \(X\to\infty\), and \(Y=o(X)\); the decisive test below takes \(X=P\) along primes and \(Y=X^{3/4}\), within the actual parameter range of Theorem 1.

Theorem3 states the exact Bessel series M_k(y)=alpha*sqrt(y)*sum_{d,s>=1}Q(d)J_{k-1}(4*pi*s*sqrt(y)/d)/s, followed by the leading coefficient alpha*(-1)^(k/2-1)*sqrt(2/pi) multiplying y^(1/4) F(sqrt(y)).

Fixed even integer k>=2; y>0 and y tends to infinity. A_p=p^4-2p^2-p+1; Q(d)=mu(d)^2 product_{p|d} p^2/A_p. alpha has the same positive normalization in both displays; J_nu is the standard Bessel function. Q(d)>=0,Q(1)=1,Q(d)=O(d^-2), since every local factor is positive and product_p p^4/A_p converges.
